- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and prices are falling, model often underestimates drop; adjust downward by 2–5% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show low sentiment and flat/declining prices, forecast should not rise above 1–2% above recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period reversals; if sentiment turns positive after 15–20 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), model tends to forecast flat or slightly upward; if true outcome shows volatility, add ±1–2% volatility buffer to forecast.
